answer: Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a juniper index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Because the garden index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the zephyr audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 20 aliases therefore needs 20 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
